metadata.name: useradd
metadata.displayName: useradd - Create a new user account

installation.note: useradd is a core admin command; on Debian/Ubuntu adduser is often preferred (wrapper around useradd)

overview.summary: useradd creates a new user account by adding an entry to /etc/passwd and related files. It can set home directory, shell, UID, and group. On Debian/Ubuntu, adduser is a friendlier wrapper that creates home dir and runs useradd.
when_to_use: Create a new system user (scripting or automation)
Add a user with specific UID, home dir, or shell
Bulk user creation with custom defaults

syntax.description: USERNAME is required. Options set home dir (-d), shell (-s), primary group (-g), supplementary groups (-G), UID (-u), etc.

options.use_case: Standard for interactive users (like adduser does)

examples.title: Create user with home and bash
examples.description: Create user jane with home directory and bash as shell
examples.use_case: Standard new user (similar to adduser jane)

examples.title: Use adduser on Debian/Ubuntu
examples.description: Interactive helper: creates user, home, and prompts for password
examples.use_case: Easier interactive user creation on Debian/Ubuntu

common_pitfalls.description: useradd does not create a home directory unless -m is used.
common_pitfalls.solution: Use useradd -m or prefer adduser on Debian/Ubuntu.

related_commands.description: Set the new user's password after useradd
